For bool: v=raw.strip().lower(); in {1,true,yes,on} -> True, {0,false,no,off} -> False, else raise. For int/float use int(raw.strip())/float(raw.strip()). Catch ValueError and raise ConfigError(f"bad value {raw!r} for {source}") from None, where source is 'section.key' for file values and the variable name for env values. (b) Change signature to load(path=None, env=None). Start from copy.deepcopy(DEFAULTS). If path is not None, read the INI file as now (keep unknown sections/keys as raw strings, known keys coerced with source f'{section}.{key}'). If env is None use os.environ (import os). (c) After the file, iterate over DEFAULTS sections and keys (do not parse env names): name = f'APP_{section.upper()}__{key.upper()}'; raw = env.get(name); skip if None or raw.strip()=='' ; else settings[section][key] = _coerce(default, raw, name). This gives exact-case matching and ignores unknown sections/keys/file-only keys/wrong separators automatically. An empty/whitespace env var for a str key is also treated as unset. Do not mutate DEFAULTS (deepcopy already). Add unit tests in tests/test_settings.py: path=None gives defaults and a fresh dict (mutating result doesn't change DEFAULTS); env overrides file overrides default; APP_DATABASE__POOL_SIZE -> int; bool values (true/Yes/ON/0/off, whitespace, 'maybe' invalid); float; lowercase var name ignored; unknown section/key/file-only key/single-underscore ignored; empty and whitespace env keeps file value with no error; ConfigError message contains 'APP_SERVER__PORT' for env and 'server.port' for file; ConfigError is a ValueError; file bool 'false' yields False; env=None uses os.environ (patch it).
